question: On a standard pure tone audiogram, which statement correctly describes the axes and conventional symbols used?

answers.text: The x-axis shows hearing level in dB HL with 0 dB at the bottom; the y-axis shows frequency in Hz

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The axes are reversed in this option. Frequency (Hz) is on the x-axis (250 to 8000 Hz, left to right), and hearing level in dB HL is on the y-axis. Additionally, 0 dB HL is at the TOP of the y-axis (representing normal threshold), and worsening hearing is plotted downward — not at the bottom.

answers.text: Frequency in Hz is on the x-axis (250–8000 Hz); hearing level in dB HL is on the y-axis with 0 dB at the top (normal) and higher dB values (worse hearing) plotted downward; right ear AC = red circle (O), left ear AC = blue cross (X)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The audiogram convention is: x-axis = frequency (low to high, 250 to 8000 Hz), y-axis = hearing level (0 at top = normal; downward = worse). Right ear air conduction is plotted as red circles (O); left ear as blue crosses (X). Bone conduction uses < and > symbols. Remembering these conventions is essential for accurate audiogram interpretation.

answers.text: Right ear is plotted in blue; left ear in red; air conduction uses triangles and bone conduction uses circles

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The colour convention is the opposite. Right ear = red (mnemonic: Red for Right), Left ear = blue. Air conduction uses O (right) and X (left); bone conduction uses < (right, pointing toward the ear) and > (left). Triangles are not a standard audiogram symbol.

answers.text: A 4 kHz dip on the audiogram with recovery at 8 kHz is the audiological pattern of conductive hearing loss

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A 4 kHz notch (dip at 4 kHz with partial recovery at 8 kHz) is the signature of noise-induced hearing loss (NIHL) — a sensorineural pattern. Conductive hearing loss produces a flat or low-frequency audiometric pattern with an air-bone gap, not a high-frequency notch.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember the audiogram axes: frequency (Hz) on x-axis, dB HL on y-axis with 0 at top. Red = right ear (O for air conduction), Blue = left ear (X for air conduction). A 4 kHz notch = NIHL, not CHL.
Well done. Axis orientation and colour-symbol conventions are the foundation of audiogram reading. Right = red circles, Left = blue crosses — a frequently tested detail.
